items.title: A Randomized Controlled Trial of a Digital Stepped-Care Program to Reduce Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms Among Long-Term Care Workers With Psychological Distress: The REPICAL Study.
items.authors: González-Spinoglio L, Esplugues-Tormo M, Giné-Vázquez I, Rodeiro-Boliart J, Aguilar-Ortiz S, Ayuso-Mateos JL, McGreevy KR, Mediavilla R, Roos R, Sijbrandij M, Witteveen AB, Haro JM, Felez-Nobrega M.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Long-term care workers (LTCWs), encompassing those in long-term care facilities and home-care settings, constitute a particularly vulnerable population to psychological distress. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a digital stepped-care program, adapted from two World Health Organization (WHO) psychological interventions-Doing What Matters in Times of Stress (DWM) and Problem Management Plus (PM+)-in reducing anxiety and depressive symptoms among LTCWs.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted. Participants were LTCWs from Catalonia (Spain) experiencing psychological distress (Kessler Psychological Distress Scale, K10 ≥ 16). All participants received Psychological First Aid (PFA), and those in the intervention group subsequently received the digital stepped-care program: DWM as step 1, and if psychological distress persisted (K10 ≥ 16), PM + as step 2. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in self-reported depressive and anxiety symptoms at week 21 (2-month post-program follow-up), measured using the Patient Health Questionnaire-Anxiety and Depression Scale (PHQ-ADS). Secondary outcomes included depressive and anxiety symptoms measured separately, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms, and health-related quality of life (HR-QoL; measured using PHQ-9, 7-item Generalized Anxiety Disorder [GAD-7] scale, PCL-5, and EuroQol 5-dimensional descriptive system-5-level [EQ-5D-5L], respectively).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Between October 2022 and May 2024, 165 participants were randomized (intervention: n  = 83; control: n  = 82). At week 21, depressive and anxiety symptoms were significantly lower in the intervention group, with moderate to large effect sizes (mean difference = 4.2, 95% CI: 1.1-7.3; Standardized effect size [SES] = 0.8, 95% CI: 0.1-1.4). Secondary outcomes also showed significantly greater improvement in the intervention group, except for HR-QoL, for which no differences were found.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This study provides evidence supporting the effectiveness of a digital and scalable stepped-care program to support LTCWs' mental health. These robust findings may inform occupational and public health strategies for supporting LTCWs' experiencing psychological distress. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05526235.

items.title: Bipolar Disorder XI: Continuous Decline of Lithium Response Inversely Correlated to Time Before Drug Administration in Relation to Onset of a Bipolar Disorder.
items.authors: Nylander PO, Lexne E, Lehman C, Brudin L, Bengtsson F.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a severe disease affecting 1% of the general population. BD comprises recurrent depressive, hypomanic, and manic episodes. BD occurs as type I (BDI) and type II (BDII). In this study, we investigated the duration of illness before lithium treatment started in BDI and BDII.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A long-term follow-up study of 192 patients with BD (diagnosed following DSM-IV criteria) were collected from lithium dispensaries. Patients with BDI and BDII were divided according to lithium response.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: We found that patients with BD responded better to lithium if the treatment was introduced early after diagnosis compared with when treatment was started later in the course of the disease. From the diagnosis of BD, BDI was in general introduced earlier to lithium treatment compared with BDII. Logistic regression analysis showed that a continuous decline in lithium response was associated with the time lag before drug administration in relation to onset of the BD. To the best of our knowledge, we can for the first time report that lithium response is associated with a continuous decrease over time from the onset of BD until the drug treatment is started.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: A short duration of illness before introduction of lithium treatment is a predictor of better lithium response regardless of whether BDI or BDII is present. Lithium response seems to gradually decline with an increasing duration of illness before lithium treatment is started.

items.title: Impact of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists on Mental Health: A Systematic Review of Psychiatric Safety and Antidepressant Potential.
items.authors: Quadir A, Devi R, Jad Allah B, Haider A, Shaikh SS, Botsa KN.

sections.text: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly used for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, but concerns about their mental health effects have been raised. Early safety reports linked them to suicidal thoughts and worsening depression; however, evidence remained mixed and unclear. A systematic search was conducted across three databases for studies published between 2021 and May 2026. Out of 617 records identified, 11 studies were finally included after quality checks using appropriate appraisal tools based on study design. This review was not prospectively registered. Data from over 4.9 million patients across eleven primary studies showed that GLP-1RAs did not increase psychiatric risk overall. Ten out of eleven primary studies confirmed either safety or protective psychiatric effects. Increased psychiatric risk was seen in one obesity-specific study; this may partly reflect surveillance or detection bias, though this was not directly tested. Only one of the 11 included studies directly measured mood using validated questionnaires and found that semaglutide was associated with lower (better) depression and anxiety scores. GLP-1 receptor agonists appear to maintain a safe neuropsychiatric profile, with an emerging signal that mood may benefit, currently limited to a single scale-based study among those formally included; most existing evidence remains diagnostic-code-based rather than scale-based. For T2DM patients with stable mood disorders, there is no justification for withholding these medications. For weight management, clinicians may consider baseline mental health screening before starting treatment. Future research must use validated continuous mood rating tools rather than administrative diagnostic codes to properly measure psychological benefits.

items.title: A cross-sectional study examining the reliability and invariance of the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21) across ten countries/regions.
items.authors: Chen XM, Li Y, Pramukti I, Ahorsu DK, Kukreti S, Chen JK, Gan WY, Ruckwongpatr K, Gupta R, Lin CK, Tran D, le An P, Griffiths MD, Chen IH, Lin CY, Malas O.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21) is widely used to assess psychological symptoms among university students. However, its factor structure remains inconsistent, and few studies have employed advanced modeling approaches such as exploratory structural equation modeling (ESEM), particularly in cross-cultural contexts.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: The present study evaluated the factor structure of the DASS-21 by comparing five models: unidimensional, oblique three-factor, bifactor, three-factor ESEM, and bifactor ESEM. For the best-fitting model, internal consistency and measurement invariance across cultural, linguistic, and demographic groups were further examined.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Using secondary data from an international mental health project, this cross-sectional study analyzed responses from 12,059 university students ( M  = 20.37 years, SD  = 1.98; age range: 18-34; 36.6% men and 63.4% women) across ten distinct countries/regions: Mainland China, Ghana, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Spain, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The three-factor ESEM model showed the best fit across the ten countries/regions with acceptable fit indices, satisfactory internal consistency (McDonald's ω  > 0.70), and acceptable internal structural validity evidence. Measurement invariance testing supported configural and metric invariance across all ten countries/regions, whereas scalar invariance was not achieved, limiting direct cross-cultural comparisons. This pattern was also observed across the seven language groups. In contrast, scalar invariance was established across age, gender, data collection mode (online versus offline), and pandemic timing (onset versus post-COVID-19), further highlighting potential cultural and linguistic influences on DASS-21 responses.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: These findings support the DASS-21's robust internal structure and reliability across diverse student populations, while emphasizing caution in cross-cultural comparisons.

items.title: Association of anxiety, depressive symptoms, and inflammatory indices with cardiometabolic multimorbidity.
items.authors: Zhang M, Guo X, Ma X, Jia J, Zhang H, Wang D, Zhang X, Ma Y, Li X.

sections.text: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) represents a major global public health challenge associated with increased mortality and reduced quality of life. While psychological distress (including anxiety and depression) and systemic inflammation have each been linked to individual cardiometabolic conditions, their combined associations with multimorbidity remain insufficiently understood. Previous literature suggests interrelationships between psychological symptoms and inflammation, but the temporal direction of these relationships cannot be examined in the present cross-sectional analysis. This cross-sectional study included 5903 community-dwelling adults in Tangshan, China. Demographic, lifestyle, and mental health data were collected via structured questionnaires; anxiety and depression were assessed using the GAD-7 and PHQ-9 scales. Five inflammatory indices (NLR, PLR, SII, LNR, NPR) were derived from routine blood tests, and CMM was defined as the coexistence of ≥2 cardiometabolic conditions. Statistical analyses included multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline modelling, interaction analyses, and sensitivity analyses. The sample included 44.49% males and 55.51% females, with an overall CMM prevalence of 15.2%. Anxiety (OR = 1.15, 95% CI: 1.00-1.28) and depression (OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.03-1.53) were associated with higher odds of prevalent CMM. In the fully adjusted model, higher tertiles of NLR, PLR, SII, LNR, and NPR were associated with CMM. Additional exploratory component-based analyses showed that standardized natural log(1+x)-transformed neutrophil and platelet counts remained associated with CMM in mutually adjusted models, whereas lymphocyte count did not. Exploratory discrimination analyses showed limited single-marker performance for anxiety or depressive symptoms across CMM strata (AUC range, 0.488-0.574), and adding inflammatory ratios or blood-cell components to common clinical determinants produced only small AUC changes (Delta AUC range, 0.001-0.020). These findings suggest that anxiety symptoms, depressive symptoms, and blood-cell-derived inflammatory indices are associated with prevalent cardiometabolic multimorbidity. However, the exploratory discrimination analyses indicated limited incremental or stand-alone discriminatory performance; therefore, these indices should not be interpreted as diagnostic or screening tools. Because this study was cross-sectional and observational, causal and predictive interpretations are not warranted.

items.title: Postpartum Depression Following a Substance-Exposed Pregnancy: The Role of Age, Race/Ethnicity, and Mental Health History.
items.authors: Aguilar N, Manzo MC, Fakhoury P, Surma J.

sections.text: Background and objective Postpartum depression (PPD) affects 13-19% of postpartum individuals and is one of the most prevalent complications of pregnancy, with significant consequences for maternal and child well-being. Research suggests that maternal age, ethnic minority status, and a history of depression are predictors of PPD. Nearly one-third of substance users also experience PPD, yet it is unclear how age, race/ethnicity, and mental health history predict PPD in this already at-risk population. This study aimed to examine the impact of age, race/ethnicity, and depression history on the development of PPD among individuals who used substances during pregnancy.  Methods A medical chart review was conducted at two university-affiliated pediatric practices in the Midwestern United States. Eligible participants were those with available maternal prenatal and delivery records, pediatric medical records through age three years, and biochemically confirmed prenatal substance use. The primary outcome was PPD, assessed primarily using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale with a score ≥ 10 through six months postpartum and/or a documented maternal report of a postpartum depression diagnosis or treatment. Results Of 255 participants, 30.19% experienced PPD. Private medical insurance holders (a proxy for higher socioeconomic status (SES)) were twice as likely to develop PPD (odds ratio (OR) = 1.96, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.09-4.28), while marijuana use increased the risk by nearly 3.4-fold (OR = 3.4, 95% CI: 1.66-6.96). Black women were nearly two and a half times more likely than White, non-Hispanic women to develop PPD, and women who reported another race or mixed race were more than four times more likely to develop PPD. A history of mental health conditions predicted a non-significant, fourfold increase in PPD risk. Age was not a significant predictor. Marijuana use and higher SES were the strongest predictors of PPD in this substance-exposed population. Conclusions Marijuana use during pregnancy, race/ethnicity, and private insurance status were independent predictors of PPD in this substance-exposed cohort. Age and pre-pregnancy mental health history were not significant in the adjusted analysis. These findings highlight the need for targeted maternal mental health screening and further research on ascertainment differences by SES.

items.authors: Zhuo C, Zhang Q, Song H, Zou J, Li R, Ma X, Chen X, Li Y, Yang L, Wang L, Li C, Tian H.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Amitriptyline, mirtazapine, and escitalopram are effective antidepressants for treating major depressive disorder (MDD). Our study aimed to use computational biology to understand the mechanisms for the similarities and differences in efficacies and side effects of these drugs.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Potential targets for MDD and the three drugs were obtained using public databases. Venn diagrams and protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed. Drug-target-pathway (D-T-P) networks were built using Cytoscape, and core targets were filtered using CytoNCA and CytoHubba plugins. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analyses were conducted using the Database for Annotation, Visualization, and Integrated Discovery. Ligand compounds and receptor proteins were processed with PyMOL and AutoDock. The binding of amitriptyline, mirtazapine, and escitalopram with core targets was predicted by molecular docking using AutoDock Vina. The results were visualized using PyMOL and protein-ligand interaction profiler (PLIP).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Forty-eight overlapping targets and 66, 50, and 30 individual targets for MDD treatment were identified for amitriptyline, mirtazapine, and escitalopram, respectively. Critical pathways included "Neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction," "Calcium signaling pathway," and "Serotonergic synapse." Key targets, indicating a wide range of effects on cellular activities and signaling mechanisms, included D(2) dopamine receptor (DRD2), CYP2D6, monoamine oxidase type B (MAOB), solute carrier family 6 member 3 (SLC6A3), solute carrier family 6 member 4 (SLC6A4), 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 2C (HTR2C), and CHRNA4. MAOB had the highest binding affinity with amitriptyline, followed by SLC6A4 and DRD2. Binding stability was enhanced by salt bridges and π-stacking interactions. Mirtazapine formed strong binding affinities with HTR2C, SLC6A4, and CHRNA4 through hydrogen bonds and π-stacking interactions. Escitalopram exhibited the highest affinity for SLC6A3, followed by HTR2C.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: All three drugs regulated serotonin, norepinephrine (NE), and dopamine, but target specificity, pathways, and binding patterns differed. Amitriptyline exhibited stronger antidepressant effects and broader mechanisms but a higher risk of side effects. Mirtazapine's dual mechanism regulates broad targets with reliable efficacy and fewer side effects. Escitalopram selectively acts on serotonin-related targets, with narrow actions and potentially fewer side effects. These findings align with the clinical profiles of the antidepressant efficacy and side effects.

items.title: Patient-reported symptom profiles in vitamin B_12 deficiency and pernicious anemia: a cross-sectional study using latent class analysis.
items.authors: Morris BM, Thain A, Schweiger BC, Nexø E, McCaddon A, Wolffenbuttel BHR, Green R, Alpers DH, Dib MJ, Visser P, Burchell K, Ahmadi KR, Reynolds AW.

sections.text: Pernicious anemia is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by impaired of vitamin B_12 absorption and deficiency. Current diagnostic approaches rely on laboratory biomarkers with limitations in sensitivity and specificity, leading to diagnostic uncertainty and potentially delayed and/or suboptimal treatment. The 2024 NICE guidelines acknowledge that treatment frequency should be guided by individual symptom response rather than current one-size-fits-all schedules; however, the symptom heterogeneity underpinning this recommendation remains poorly characterized. We conducted secondary analysis of symptom survey data from 1,117 members of the Pernicious Anaemia Society (PAS) collected between August 2010 and November 2012. We applied latent class analysis (LCA) to 46 self-reported indicators comprising demographic characteristics, symptoms, and comorbid conditions, to identify distinct symptom-based subtypes and assess whether such subgroups can inform more tailored management of PA. Associations between symptom subtypes and diagnostic test results, age when symptoms first started, symptom duration, and treatment satisfaction were examined using chi-square and Fisher's exact tests. The best model included three distinct symptom subtypes: High Burden ( n  = 334, 29.9%), Moderate Burden ( n  = 613, 54.9%), and Low Burden ( n  = 170, 15.2%). The High Burden subtype exhibited fatigue (99.4%), cognitive dysfunction (97.9% memory loss), neurological manifestations (95.5% clumsiness), and suicidal thoughts (41.6%). Intrinsic factor antibody (IFA) status did not differ significantly across subtypes ( χ ^2 = 1.04, df = 2, p  = 0.593). Age at symptom onset differed significantly across subtypes ( p  = 0.002), with the Low Burden subtype overrepresented in older age groups. The High Burden subtype had the longest diagnostic delays (56.9% >2 years). Standard three-monthly injections showed low satisfaction across all classes (High Burden: 8.5%, Moderate Burden: 23.7%, Low Burden: 30.7%). Symptom-based stratification identifies clinically meaningful subgroups independent of IFA status, supporting tailored, symptom-guided treatment rather than the current piecemeal approach. The inverse association between high symptom burden and age of onset warrants clinical attention. The co-occurrence of markedly elevated rates of depression and suicidal thoughts in the High Burden subtype suggest that integrated mental health assessments should form part of routine clinical management.

items.title: Early socially isolated rats of both sexes reduce alcohol consumption and seeking by the Galanin (1-15) and naltrexone combination.
items.authors: Flores-Gómez M, Cantero-García N, Pineda-Gómez JP, Flores-Burgess A, Díaz-Cabiale Z, Millón C.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) is a psychiatric condition whose severity can be amplified by social factors, such as social isolation, particularly during adolescence, which exacerbates development of AUD in adulthood. Our previous studies have demonstrated that the Galanin (1-15) fragment [GAL (1-15)] reduces alcohol seeking and consumption. Furthermore, the combination of GAL (1-15) with Naltrexone (NTX)-an approved but moderately effective treatment for AUD- potentiates reduced alcohol intake and seeking behavior, showing interaction with the opioid system.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: Previous studies on the effects of GAL (1-15) on AUD have been conducted mainly in male animals, leaving the effects on females largely unexplored despite the well-established sex differences in alcohol use disorder. Therefore, this study introduces early-life social isolation as a critical environmental vulnerability factor for adult alcohol abuse and evaluates these mechanisms in female subjects for the first time. Specifically, we investigate the combined effects of GAL (1-15)+NTX on alcohol consumption and seeking in male and female adolescent-isolated rats, along with associated changes in mesolimbic gene expression.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In socially isolated male and female rats, we evaluated GAL (1-15)+NTX in terms of voluntary alcohol intake (two-bottle choice) and reward-seeking behavior (self-administration). We analyzed transcriptional changes in C-Fos, MOR, dopamine and galanin receptors in the ventral tegmental area and nucleus accumbens.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Social isolation moderately increased ethanol intake and operant alcohol responding in both sexes. GAL (1-15)+NTX significantly reduced operant responding in isolated rats of both sexes, but reduced alcohol consumption only in males, with no significant effect in females at the tested doses. These effects were associated with alterations in C-Fos, MOR and dopamine receptor expression, suggesting that there is an association between molecular changes related to the mesolimbic and opioid systems and the observed reduction in alcohol-seeking behavior and consumption, even in a model of early social isolation.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: These findings suggest that GAL (1-15)+NTX could be explored further as a potential strategy in AUD research, particularly in socially vulnerable contexts.

items.title: Predicting multiple mental health outcomes in adolescents using explainable machine learning models.
items.authors: Dong X, Meng J, Wang P, Yan C, Liu X.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Adolescent mental health problems, including depression, anxiety, and stress, are an increasing public health concern, yet the factors associated with different mental health outcomes may vary across domains. This study investigated shared and outcome-specific predictive features of depression, anxiety, perceived stress, and psychological well-being using explainable machine learning models.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 1,088 adolescents aged 13-18 years recruited from secondary schools in Wuhan, China, using multistage cluster sampling. Participants completed validated measures of emotional dysregulation, loneliness, social media addiction, self-esteem, sleep quality, academic stress, family support, physical activity, and mental health outcomes. Four algorithms-linear regression, support vector regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost-were trained using an 80/20 train-test split with five-fold cross-validation, and model performance was evaluated using test-set R², RMSE, and MAE. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to examine feature contributions. To minimize target leakage, outcome-specific feature sets were used, with PSQI and RSES excluded from the depression model because of direct or substantial conceptual overlap with PHQ-9 content, and PSQI excluded from the well-being model because of overlap with WHO-5 content.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: XGBoost showed the strongest out-of-sample predictive performance across all four outcomes, explaining 49% of the variance in depression (R² = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.44-0.53; RMSE = 3.52; MAE = 2.81), 55% in anxiety (R² = 0.55, 95% CI: 0.50-0.59; RMSE = 3.04; MAE = 2.47), 60% in perceived stress (R² = 0.60, 95% CI: 0.56-0.64; RMSE = 3.71; MAE = 2.87), and 50% in psychological well-being (R² = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.45-0.54; RMSE = 3.38; MAE = 2.68).

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: Emotional dysregulation and loneliness were consistently among the most influential features, while academic stress, family support, social media addiction, self-esteem, and sleep quality showed outcome-specific contributions. SHAP rankings for the depression model were stable across five-fold cross-validation, with emotional dysregulation and loneliness consistently occupying the highest ranks.

items.title: Digital psychoeducational rehabilitation supported by serious games for psychiatric inpatients: a protocol study.
items.authors: Gigantesco A, Volpe U, Calamandrei G, Orsolini L, Premici A, Deplano V, Re DD, Cascavilla I, Brescianini S, Camoni L.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD) are characterized by impairments in thought, perception, emotion, and behavior, leading to reduced personal and social functioning. While pharmacological treatments have limited efficacy on negative and cognitive symptoms, psychosocial interventions play a crucial role but remain difficult for many patients to access, particularly among youths. Digital interventions, particularly serious games, offer a promising approach to enhance recovery by improving accessibility, engagement, and motivation. The present protocol study aims to develop and preliminary evaluate serious games as a complementary tool to standard psychoeducational interventions for young SSD patients. The primary objective is to evaluate the feasibility of some serious games in a real-world clinical setting. Secondary objectives are to explore whether the addition of those serious games to a standard psychoeducational intervention leads to a greater improvement in global functioning, emotion dysregulation, severity of general psychopathology and other clinical or functional outcomes.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A quasi-experimental, non-randomized study with a historical control group will be conducted at the Unit of Clinical Psychiatry, Polytechnic University of Marche (Italy), involving patients aged 15-24 years diagnosed with SSD and related disorders, including at-risk mental states. Participants will be inpatients who had received a standard conventional psychoeducational program (control group) and inpatients who will receive the same program supplemented with serious games (experimental group). These games delivered both via web-based platform and smartphone application, simulate real-life scenarios and reinforce learning through interactive and repetitive exercises.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: We expect the integration of serious games to be feasible and well accepted, enhancing engagement, adherence, mental health literacy, and the consolidation and transfer of skills acquired through standard psychoeducation, with potential improvements in global functioning and psychopathological symptoms.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This approach may represent a scalable and innovative strategy to improve the recovery and long-term outcomes in youth with SSD and related disorders admitted to an acute psychiatric setting.

items.title: How have contemporary studies evaluating self-help digital mental health interventions for young people monitored and reported on adverse events and harms?: a systematic scoping review.
items.authors: Munir S, Dallison S, Padley H, Fung HM, Perry G, Hall CL, Loades ME.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Many digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) can be effective in reducing symptoms of common mental health problems in young people and can overcome many barriers to accessing treatment. These are most scalable when offered as self-help. However, all mental health interventions have the potential to cause harm, and this should be monitored.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.text: To identify current practices and gaps in safety reporting, we systematically mapped how adverse events have been monitored and reported in contemporary studies evaluating self-guided DMHIs for young people.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: We conducted a systematic scoping review. Two databases were searched for relevant studies published between 2019 and 2024. We synthesised the findings narratively, drawing on content analysis to identify patterns.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: We included 37 studies, 12 (32.4%) of which described how they assessed adverse events (AEs). AEs were identified through worsening on wellbeing/psychometric measures, measures of risk and suicidal ideation/behaviour, participants self-identifying AEs, and parental reporting of AEs. Additionally, some studies reported on the proportion of participants experiencing AEs, with 8 (21.6%) studies reporting adverse events as an outcome. The most commonly occurring AEs reported were hospitalisation, treatment non-response, depressive symptoms, and significant worsening of symptoms (each 5.4% respectively). Other AEs reported were self-harm, substance misuse, anxiety symptoms, suicidal thoughts, suicide attempt and headaches (each 2.7% respectively).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Despite the potential for adverse events to occur while young people are using self-guided DMHIs, our review highlighted a gap in the monitoring of and reporting of adverse events in these kinds of intervention studies.

items.title: Efficacy, management of adverse effects and relapse forms after obsessive-compulsive disorder surgery: The first Egyptian and Arab cohort.
items.authors: Hamdi H, Aref H, Kamel M.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The aim of this study was to investigate the outcome of neurosurgery for mental illness in a cohort of Egyptian/Arab patients with treatment-resistant obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Sixteen patients were recruited from various psychiatric clinics. All participants met DSM-5 criteria for OCD and had failed extensive trials of psychiatric medications and psychotherapies. Eligibility criteria focused on significant distress and functional impairment, as well as a Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (YBOCS) score greater than 30. Patients underwent either cingulotomy or capsulotomy and were followed monthly beginning immediately after surgery. Follow-up assessment evaluated OCD symptom severity, depression, anxiety, functional status, and both immediate and delayed postoperative adverse effects.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: At the most recent follow-up (median: 19, range: 6 months - 25 months), 56.25% (9/16) of patients achieved at least a partial response, including 8 responders and 1 partial responder. Significant reductions in YBOCS, Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), and Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale scores were recorded, suggesting that psychosurgery may be associated with improvement in OCD symptoms. However, because this was a noncontrolled study, causality between surgery and clinical improvement cannot be established. Immediate adverse effects were mild, transient, and observed in 37.5% (6/16) of patients. Delayed adverse effects were reported by 68.75% (11/16) of the total cohort and were predominantly characterized by recurrence of the initial OCD symptoms (9/16), often accompanied by depressive symptoms. Notably, two-thirds of patients who experienced symptom relapse were subsequently managed successfully with pharmacotherapy and behavioral therapy.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Both cingulotomy and capsulotomy may be associated with significant reductions in OCD symptom severity, as well as improvements in depression and anxiety among patients with treatment-resistant OCD. Although relapse of OCD symptoms during follow-up was common, close monthly monitoring immediately after surgery and ongoing management were effective in restoring clinical improvement in many patients. As the first study of its kind conducted in Egypt and the Arab world, these findings also highlight the unique cultural challenges encountered in introducing psychiatric surgery within this setting.

items.title: Mucosal microbiota and intraepithelial lymphocyte remodeling link maternal immune activation to neuroimmune outcomes in female and male offspring.
items.authors: Pereira-Santos AR, Jesus-Faria S, Candeias E, Maranha A, Tiago I, Rodrigues-Santos P, Empadinhas N, Cardoso SM.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Maternal immune activation (MIA) is associated with increased risk for neurodevelopmental disorders, including schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorder, yet its long-term impact on intestinal immune-microbial programming remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced MIA drives persistent alterations in the offspring mucosal immune environment, with a focus on intraepithelial lymphocytes, mucosa-associated microbiota, systemic cytokines, and prefrontal cortical immune-related readouts.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: MIA was induced in wild-type BALB/cByJ mice via intraperitoneal LPS injection at gestational day 12.5. Male and female offspring were assessed at 10 weeks of age for gut, systemic, and prefrontal cortex (PFC) immune alterations.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: MIA offspring displayed a regionally restricted intestinal immune signature, with more pronounced alterations in the ileum than in the colon. Ileal changes included increased inflammatory cytokine signaling and remodeling of IEL populations, particularly TCRγδ CD8αα cells, together with changes in TCRαβ IEL subsets. Analysis of the mucosa-associated microbiome revealed parallel changes in ileal microbial community structure, including alterations in segmented filamentous bacteria and Lactobacillus. These mucosal alterations co-occurred with increased plasma IL-6 in both female and male offspring, while plasma IL-17 was selectively increased in females. In the PFC, MIA was associated with cytokine changes and divergent microglial morphological profiles, suggesting that prenatal immune challenge produces neuroimmune alterations that may differ in sex, timing, magnitude, or cellular expression.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Collectively, these findings identify the mucosa-associated microbiota-IEL interface as a previously underexplored component of MIA-induced immune remodeling. Our study provides an integrated framework in which persistent ileal immune and microbial alterations co-occur with systemic inflammation and cortical neuroimmune changes in MIA offspring, supporting future mechanistic studies of gut-brain immune communication in neurodevelopmental disorders.

items.title: Role of the ketogenic diet in neurodevelopmental disorders: neuroprotection and clinical practice.
items.authors: Sun L, Qu L, Gao S, Chen J, Wu P, Wang H.

sections.text: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), occur early in life and affect cognitive and behavioral health and motor development. While hereditary factors contribute to the development of ASD, recent research has shown that environmental factors, notably nutritional factors, play important roles in determining the severity and expression of symptoms. The ketogenic diet (KD), a high-fat, low-carbohydrate dietary strategy, has well-established therapeutic significance, particularly in the management of epilepsy. Currently, the KD has recently gained popularity beyond therapeutic treatment, becoming popular as a general health and lifestyle option for healthy people. However, despite its long history, the effects of KD consumption on the development of NDDs are uncertain. This review highlights current literature on the effects of maternal KD on child brain development and NDD development, emphasizing the potential relevance of the KD in treating NDDs. We discuss the therapeutic implications of KD consumption and highlight the known effects of maternal KD on NDD development in children, potentially improving our understanding of NDD treatment. Assessments of the safety of KD and its long-term effects on the developing nervous system should be prioritized in future studies to help evaluate the feasibility, safety, and implementation of the KD in treating NDDs.

items.title: Strategies to enhance engagement in CBT for adult ADHD: an innovation tournament with stakeholders.
items.authors: Sibley MH, Shafiee M, Knouse LE.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: Adults with ADHD report challenges engaging in cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT). This study investigates practices that might be applied to improve intervention fit and therapeutic engagement of CBT for adults with ADHD.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: We conducted an Innovation Tournament (IT) and member checking with participants ( N= 102) who were adults with ADHD and mental health practitioners who regularly treat adults with ADHD. Go-Zone plots were utilized to identify strategies with the highest feasibility and importance as well as strategies with low feasibility and/or importance that might be candidates for de-implementation. Barriers to CBT engagement and practitioner implementation of practices were also evaluated qualitatively.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A range of engagement barriers were identified, chief among them practitioner low understanding of ADHD (44.4%) and lack of attention to relevant impairments (33.3%). The highest rated focal areas for CBT were task management, organization, planning, and prioritization, emotion regulation strategies, responding to negative/maladaptive thoughts, anti-procrastination and self-motivation strategies, and long-term goal setting. Top recommendations for engagement strategies include ensuring high therapist knowledge of ADHD and 17 elements consistent with Motivational Interviewing. Some practices commonly found in CBTs for ADHD were rated as unpopular with stakeholders, most notably providing weekly ratings of ADHD symptoms as progress monitoring. Some practices rated as important to adults with ADHD were rated as not feasible to practitioners-most notably reducing shame and nurturing confidence. Implementation barriers identified were primarily related to low practitioner knowledge and skills, but also sometimes systemic constraints on practice.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Implementation of recommended practices noted in this study should be tested empirically to understand the extent to which they increase engagement and effectiveness over standard practice.

items.title: The #chatsafe Youth Participation Model: Evaluating Participatory Workshops Involving Young People in the Design of Suicide Prevention Initiatives.
items.authors: La Sala L, Carrotte ER, Cooper C, Lamblin M, Brown E, Robinson J.
items.journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: #chatsafe is a programme aiming to empower young people to communicate safely on social media about self-harm and suicide. This study aimed to assess the feasibility, acceptability, safety, and impact associated with attending a #chatsafe participatory workshop, using the #chatsafe Youth Participation Model. The workshops aimed to educate young people on safe communication practices and gather their insights to inform new #chatsafe social media intervention content.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Quantitative data were collected in a pre- and post-workshop survey using bespoke items measuring perceived feasibility, acceptability, and safety of the workshops, and self-efficacy in communicating online about suicide. Qualitative data were collected during the workshop (via participant feedback, field notes, audio recordings, and facilitator debriefing notes) and in open-text responses in the post-workshop survey.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Nine workshops were held with 107 participants (age M = 19.7 years, SD = 2.7 years). Two thirds (64.5%) reported lifetime suicidal thoughts. Eighty-seven (81.3%) completed both the pre- and post-workshop survey. Feedback was positive, with 94.3% of participants reporting satisfaction with the workshop, 96.5% reported enjoying the workshop, and no adverse events were recorded. There was a significant increase in confidence when communicating online about suicide following participation in a #chatsafe workshop, z = -5.99, p < 0.001. Workshop insights informed two national Australian #chatsafe Instagram campaigns, that reached 950,000 young people and 818,000 young people respectively.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The #chatsafe workshops were highly feasible, acceptable, safe, and led to young people feeling better equipped to communicate safely online about suicide. To further encourage the involvement of young people in the design of suicide prevention, mental health, and similar initiatives, a #chatsafe Youth Participation Toolkit is publicly available for other researchers and outlines the steps taken to plan, conduct, and translate the outcomes of such workshops.

sections.heading: Lived experience or public contribution
sections.text: This study summarises the views of 87 young people who attended a #chatsafe participatory workshop and provided feedback. The #chatsafe Youth Participation Toolkit was also shaped by seven workshop participants who attended a subsequent focus group, which focused on what recommendations the researchers should share with others who wish to use these participatory methods in the future.

items.title: A Case of Isolated Abnormal Behavior Associated With Vitamin B12 Deficiency.
items.authors: Abdelaziz Ibrahim SA, Ahmed Mohamed SM, Al Quradaghi SA, Abdallah Ali SA, Nishan H, Mammadu M, Neffati N, Purayil NK.

sections.text: Vitamin B12 is a water-soluble nutrient found mainly in animal-derived foods. Vitamin B12 deficiency is a common condition, presenting with hematologic and neurologic abnormalities, but rarely presents as isolated psychosis in a young adult. A 28-year-old male patient was brought in for severe agitation and confusion. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe vitamin B12 deficiency (serum vitamin B12 of <73.8 pmol/L) with elevated homocysteine (25.4 umol/L) and methylmalonic acid (0.95 umol/L) levels. The patient received vitamin B12 replacement, after which his confusion and behavioral disturbances improved significantly, and further psychiatric evaluation failed to reveal a primary psychotic or mood disorder. This case highlights the importance of considering vitamin B12 deficiency in patients with isolated neuropsychiatric symptoms, even in the absence of typical macrocytosis, and demonstrates the potential for significant clinical recovery following timely treatment with vitamin supplementation.

items.title: Determinants of ADHD Health Literacy and Public Awareness of Child-Friendly City Policies in Wenzhou: A Cross-Sectional Survey.
items.authors: Ye J, Wen Y, Zhang T, Zeng Y, Jin X, Lin J, Du S, Yang X, Zhan J, Hla KWY, Shu X, Wang D.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To evaluate adult Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)-related health literacy, its determinants, and public awareness of local Child-Friendly City (CFC) policies in Wenzhou.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This study adopted a mixed-methods design. The quantitative cross-sectional survey recruited 1792 adults (≥18 years), applying a validated 9-item ADHD knowledge scale to gauge ADHD health literacy. Independent t -tests, one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and chi-square tests, factorial ANOVA, and Poisson regression respectively analyzed univariate group disparities, multivariate interactions, and independent predictors of literacy outcomes. For the qualitative strand, independent semi-structured interviews with 300 participants (including minors) were conducted to explore public perceptions and awareness of local CFC policies. Thematic analysis was adopted to synthesize interview narratives about policy understanding and dissemination.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Single-factor analysis initially revealed potential associations between educational level, occupation, attitudes toward ADHD, and having relatives or friends with ADHD were significant influencing factors in both regions (all P<0.05), with significant interactions (eg interaction of parental status, age, and educational level; all P<0.05). Yet these associations reversed after adjustment for confounders. Poisson regression, confirmed educational level (β = 0.0624), positive attitude (β = 0.0758) and do not know having relatives or friends with ADHD (β = 0.1002) as positive predictors (β = 0.1002) (all P<0.05). Regarding policy awareness, Dongtou District showed superior understanding overall compared to the Wenzhou Urban Area (all P<0.05), and professional groups (healthcare- and education-related practitioners) exhibited significantly higher awareness levels than the general public.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Wenzhou adults have moderately low ADHD health literacy with regional and social disparities. Higher educational level, positive attitude, and do not know having relatives or friends with ADHD predicted superior literacy, while female gender, urban residence, and professional identities correlate with lower levels. CFC policy awareness is inadequate. Targeted dissemination for high-priority groups and region-adapted support systems are needed.

items.title: A comparative study of traditional Chinese mind-body therapies on sleep quality, mental health, and quality of life in patients with sleep disorders: a network meta-analysis based on randomized controlled trials.
items.authors: An X.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Sleep disorders are a common clinical condition characterized primarily by difficulty falling asleep, trouble maintaining sleep, and impaired daytime functioning, with a high prevalence among adults. This condition can lead to a persistent decline in sleep quality, trigger mental health issues such as anxiety and depression, and ultimately reduce overall quality of life. Traditional Chinese mind-body exercise therapies are considered potentially effective non-pharmacological interventions due to their low risk, high accessibility, and dual mind-body regulation effects. However, the relative efficacy of different exercise therapies on sleep quality, mental health, and quality of life in patients with sleep disorders remains unclear. This study employed a web-based meta-analysis to systematically evaluate the effects of three interventions-Tai Chi, Baduanjin, and Tai Chi combined with transcranial magnetic stimulation-on three outcome measures and to rank their efficacy, aiming to provide evidence-based support for clinical decision-making.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This study conducted a systematic search of the PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane, EBSCO, and CNKI databases and included 18 randomized controlled trials that met the inclusion criteria. Outcome measures included sleep quality, mental health, and quality of life. A network meta-analysis using a random-effects model was performed to calculate standardized mean differences and 95% confidence intervals, and the cumulative ranking probability curve area was used to rank the efficacy of the interventions.

sections.heading: Result
sections.text: This study included a total of 18 randomized controlled trials. Regarding sleep quality, TCCWTMS yielded the best results (SMD = -1.15, 95% CI [-2.07, -0.22]). Regarding mental health, only the Tai Chi intervention achieved statistical significance (SMD = 0.64, 95% CI [0.07, 1.21], P = 0.03); although Baduanjin ranked first in the SUCRA ranking (92.6%), pairwise comparisons did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.07). Regarding quality of life, both Tai Chi (SMD = -0.47, 95% CI [-0.71, -0.24], P < 0.0001) and Baduanjin (SMD = -0.57, 95% CI [-0.91, -0.23], P = 0.001) were significantly effective. There were significant heterogeneous differences in the efficacy of the three interventions across different outcome measures.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This study indicates that the TCCWTMS is the most effective intervention for improving sleep quality in patients with sleep disorders. Regarding quality of life, both Baduanjin and Tai Chi demonstrated significant effects, with Baduanjin showing superior efficacy. Regarding mental health, the current evidence is insufficient to determine the optimal intervention strategy. There are significant differences in the efficacy of the three interventions across various outcome measures; clinical decisions can be made by selecting the appropriate intervention based on the patient's score needs.

items.authors: Li Q, Yin X.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Doomscrolling is persistent or repetitive engagement with predominantly negative, threatening, or distressing online information, often accompanied by difficulty disengaging. items.title: Delirium in Patients With Traumatic Brain Injury and Long-Term Cognitive Decline: A Global Federated Real World Data Analysis.
items.authors: Sabahizadeh A, Askarinejad A, Ahmadzadeh K, Mirjalili SR, Farshid K, Serio L, Tartaglia E, Proietti R, Davies R, Lip GYH.

sections.heading: Background and objective
sections.text: Delirium may occur in patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI), but this may be a marker for subsequent cognitive decline post-TBI. We aimed to compare cognitive outcomes and all-cause mortality between TBI patients with and without delirium.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX global federated research network. We compared TBI patients who developed delirium within 14 days of TBI diagnosis with those who did not. The primary outcome was the 2-year composite risk of dementia, vascular dementia and Alzheimer's disease. Secondary outcomes included dementia, vascular dementia, Alzheimer's disease and all-cause mortality. Pre-specified subgroup analyses were performed in female patients, older adults (≥ 75 years), and individuals with substance use.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: TBI patients with delirium (n = 2564; mean age, 66.6 ± 19.4 years; 59.4% male), when compared with TBI patients without delirium (n = 667,950; mean age, 48.0 ± 25.1 years; 60.3% male), had more baseline comorbidities, including psychiatric disease, cerebrovascular disease and ischemic heart disease. After propensity score matching, TBI patients with delirium, compared with those without delirium, had a higher 2-year risk of the primary composite outcome (HR, 2.47; 95% CI, 1.84-3.31), as well as dementia (HR, 2.63; 95% CI, 1.92-3.60), vascular dementia (HR, 2.76; 95% CI, 1.45-5.24) and Alzheimer's disease (HR, 2.23; 95% CI, 1.21-4.09).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Delirium following TBI is associated with an increased risk of dementia and Alzheimer's disease. Delirium post-TBI may be a marker or a contributing factor to long-term cognitive decline in TBI patients.

items.title: Risperidone-induced severe hypothermia in an elderly woman with possible prior quetiapine-associated hypothermia tolerating aripiprazole: A case report and literature review.
items.authors: Seguin A, Niknam N, Bahremand A, Masson V.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Hypothermia is a rare, potentially life-threatening adverse effect of antipsychotics, including risperidone. Defined as a core temperature<35°C (95°F), it can occur even at therapeutic doses and may be underrecognized, particularly in older adults or medically complex patients.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: An 84-year-old woman with a history of psychosis and comorbidities developed severe hypothermia (31.9°C/87.8°F) 20 days after switching from quetiapine to risperidone. Infection, endocrine abnormalities, and environmental causes were excluded. Risperidone was discontinued, and normothermia was restored within 3 days. Notably, a month prior, she had a hypothermic episode while on quetiapine in the setting of infection and prescribed opioid use despite tolerating it for 5 years. Aripiprazole was later initiated and titrated to 15 mg daily; her temperature intermittently approached 35°C/95°F without symptoms but remained stable over 4 years of follow-up without further hypothermic episodes despite experiencing infections.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: This case highlights diagnostic challenges and the potential for antipsychotic-induced hypothermia to recur across different agents in the same patient. Literature review suggests the phenomenon is more common than previously believed, particularly among older patients. Whereas risperidone and quetiapine are implicated in multiple reports, aripiprazole may be better tolerated in some predisposed individuals. Routine temperature monitoring during antipsychotic initiation and titration is warranted.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: Risperidone can cause severe hypothermia in older patients even at standard doses. Clinicians should consider alternative antipsychotics when hypothermia occurs and consider that it can recur even if confounding factors are resolved. This case supports the inclusion of temperature surveillance in antipsychotic treatment protocols for older adults.

items.title: School refusal behavior in children and adolescents: a concept analysis.
items.authors: Wang L, Li X, Li X, Lei M, Luo H, Xue B.

sections.text: School refusal behavior (SRB) is increasingly recognized across educational, pediatric, and mental health settings, yet its conceptual boundaries remain unclear, and the term is frequently conflated with school refusal, truancy, school withdrawal, school exclusion, and broader school attendance problems. This study used Walker and Avant's concept analysis method to clarify the meaning, defining attributes, antecedents, consequences, and empirical referents of SRB. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and PsycINFO were searched for English-language literature published through January 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar and manual citation searching. A total of 100 sources were included and analyzed through iterative comparison of conceptual definitions, recurrent characteristics, contextual conditions, outcomes, and indicators used in research and practice. The analysis showed that SRB has evolved from earlier anxiety-centered descriptions toward a broader behavioral and functional construct. Four defining attributes were identified: difficulty initiating, sustaining, or completing school attendance or participation; young person-expressed attendance difficulty; aversive school-related experiences or emotional distress; and heterogeneous avoidance- or reinforcement-related maintaining functions. Antecedents were distributed across individual, family, peer and interpersonal, and school-contextual domains, while consequences extended across academic, psychological, social, family, and service-related domains and may accumulate over time. Empirical identification requires the integration of observable attendance patterns, emotional, behavioral, and somatic responses, functional assessment, and contextual information from young people, caregivers, and school personnel. Moving beyond the summary of existing definitions, this analysis proposes an integrative framework that distinguishes the observable form of attendance difficulty from its emotional presentation, maintaining functions, and ecological context. SRB is therefore best understood as a persistent or recurrent, young person-expressed pattern of disrupted school attendance or participation that is clinically meaningful but cannot be reduced to a single diagnosis, cause, or attendance threshold. By clarifying what constitutes SRB and how it differs from other forms of school attendance problems, this framework may support earlier recognition of emerging attendance difficulties, more comprehensive assessment of underlying needs, and better coordination among mental health professionals, families, and schools.

items.title: Longitudinal assessment of physiological and mental health changes following acute COVID-19 in Uganda.
items.authors: Rooney JA, Sharma A, Ceasor F, Schenkel SR, Mutekanga A, Jackson PD, Kabajaasi O, Wiens MO, Hibberd PL, Arvind DK, Tonne C, Worodria W, Moschovis PP.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Recovery following acute COVID-19 varies widely, yet early recovery patterns remain understudied in Africa. Given the high burden of post-infection morbidity in resource-limited settings, there is a need to characterize recovery trajectories and identify those at risk for delayed recovery.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We enrolled 151 adults between July 2021 and July 2022 with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection from healthcare facilities in Uganda and followed them for 12 weeks. Outcomes included pulmonary function, exercise capacity, symptom burden, and mental health, and were analyzed descriptively and using mixed-effects models.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Participants with severe acute COVID-19 had the greatest impairments during recovery. At 12 weeks, forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1), diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO), and six-minute walk distance remained lower in severe versus mild cases (mean (SD): 98.45 (22.22) vs 105.26 (12.29); 78.99 (18.83) vs 107.72 (20.44); 409.28 (71.18) vs 506.82 (70.87)), consistent with adjusted models showing lower FEV1 (β = -13.10, 95% CI: -24.13, -2.07), DLCO (β = -40.75, 95% CI: -53.84, -27.66), and six-minute walk distance (β = -95.87, 95% CI: -136.66, -55.08). Continued COVID-19 and mental health symptoms were reported across all groups; mild cases had worse mental health scores (23.19 (12.65) vs 16.95 (13.98)), while severe cases had a broader range of persistent symptoms, including fatigue, breathlessness, and cognitive complaints.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: In this longitudinal study in Uganda, COVID-19 was associated with persistent physiological and psychosocial impacts, particularly among those with severe illness. Initial severity may help identify individuals at risk for delayed recovery and guide targeted post-COVID care in resource-limited settings.

items.title: Boerhaave Syndrome Caused by Pancreatitis-Induced Gastric Outlet Obstruction: A Case Report.
items.authors: Viegas V, Pais Moreira H, Sousa I, Martins D, Amado A, Santos M, Tavares A, Mendes M, Viveiros F, Pereira B.

sections.text: Boerhaave syndrome is a spontaneous transmural perforation of the esophagus, typically triggered by forceful vomiting and carrying a high mortality rate when diagnosis is delayed. We present a 56-year-old man with chronic alcohol use disorder who developed esophageal perforation through an unusual causal chain. He presented with intractable vomiting, hematemesis, and cervical subcutaneous emphysema. Computed tomography showed posterior pneumomediastinum and marked gastric and duodenal distention caused by an inflammatory cephalopancreatic mass. Elevated pancreatic enzymes confirmed acute pancreatitis. The sequence appeared to be alcoholic pancreatitis compressing the duodenum, causing gastric outlet obstruction, protracted emesis, and esophageal rupture. On the day of admission, laparoscopic primary two-layer esophagorrhaphy and gastrojejunostomy were performed to address both the perforation and the duodenal obstruction. The postoperative course was complicated by recurrent pancreatitis and bilateral pleural effusions, but serial imaging confirmed no leak at the esophageal repair or the anastomosis. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 25. Follow-up magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography excluded pancreatic malignancy and showed findings consistent with groove pancreatitis and chronic pancreatitis. This case illustrates an unusual causal chain in which acute pancreatitis led to esophageal perforation via gastric outlet obstruction and reinforces the benefit of same-day surgical repair when both the perforation and its cause can be addressed in a single procedure.

items.title: The impact of intergenerational transmission of stigma on the psychological development of minors with HIV-positive parents.
items.authors: Li C, Zhang J, Gao R, Cai L, Yang T, Wang Y, Luo F.

sections.text: With the widespread adoption of antiretroviral therapy, HIV infection has become a chronic, manageable condition, and the population of HIV-positive parents continues to grow. The stigma linked to their condition passes down to their minor children within the family. This harms the children's mental health and makes it harder to prevent and control HIV. This review explores the patterns and mechanisms of intergenerational transmission. It uses stigma theory and ecological systems theory. By examining evidence from around the world and within China, it highlights transmission features and how to adapt interventions specifically for the Chinese context. The results indicate that the stigma experienced by HIV-positive parents exhibits three-dimensional overlap, role specificity, and chronic persistence, with significant population heterogeneity. Intergenerational transmission happens through a four-level chain. It includes family communication and disclosure, parent-child attachment, and family functioning. Next, parental emotions and behaviors come into play. Finally, children's understanding and internalisation of stigma follow. This process shows a dose-response relationship with psychological harm in children. Among existing interventions, family-system-integrated interventions yield the best outcomes, supplemented by individual parental interventions, child protection measures, and social structural interventions; these must be adapted to local cultural and population characteristics. The study shows that we can intervene in the intergenerational passing of disease-related shame. Future research should include longitudinal studies, focus on specific populations, and develop multi-system collaborative intervention models to safeguard the rights of affected children and improve the comprehensive HIV/AIDS prevention and control system.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Hemiplegic gait disturbance after ischemic stroke severely impairs patients' mobility; however, existing tools still have limitations in both comprehensive evaluation and routine clinical application.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This study enrolled 15 patients with ischemic stroke and 15 healthy controls, and collected gait parameters using the CAREN system. Among these participants, 5 patients completed a 5-day continuous training regimen and participated in a longitudinal before-after comparison analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Baseline measures revealed pathological gait patterns. Post-intervention, step width, stride symmetry, and moment profiles showed short-term improvement trends.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The CAREN system can objectively quantify gait abnormalities in stroke patients and capture short-term change trends, providing a reproducible instrumental gait assessment framework. This study is exploratory in nature, its independent efficacy requires validation through large-sample randomized controlled trials.

items.title: Neuroanatomical correlates of psychiatric manifestations in Wilson disease: the role of age.
items.authors: Wang A, Xu C, Liu D, Jiang M, Li C.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To investigate gray matter volume (GMV) differences related to psychiatric manifestations in patients with Wilson disease (WD) and to examine the effect of age.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In 102 patients with WD, 3.0T T1-weighted MRI scans were analyzed using voxel-based morphometry. Patients were divided into younger (≤30 years) and older (>30 years) groups and were further grouped according to psychiatric manifestations. Patients with a UWDRS psychiatric subscale (UWDRS-PSY) score of 0 were classified as having no psychiatric manifestations, and those with a score >0 were classified as having psychiatric manifestations. Two-way ANCOVA was performed with total intracranial volume, sex, and education as covariates. Cluster-level family-wise error (FWE) correction was applied. Mean GMV values were extracted from significant caudate clusters and correlated with UWDRS-PSY scores as exploratory analyses.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Significant interactions between age group and psychiatric manifestations were found in the left insula/Rolandic operculum and right inferior temporal gyrus. Lower GMV in these regions was mainly found in younger patients with psychiatric manifestations. A main effect of psychiatric manifestations was found in the bilateral caudate nuclei, with lower GMV in patients with psychiatric manifestations. Lower caudate GMV was also associated with higher UWDRS-PSY scores.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Psychiatric manifestations in WD are associated with distinct gray matter patterns that vary with age, while bilateral caudate involvement may represent a more consistent structural correlate. These findings highlight the potential importance of considering age when examining the neuroanatomical correlates of psychiatric manifestations in WD.

items.title: Latent profile analysis and related factors for fear of progression among nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients.
items.authors: Zheng M, Wang S, Zhu Y, Wan H.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Fear of progression is a common psychological burden among nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients, persisting for many years following treatment completion. However, most existing studies focus on total scale scores and overlook the potential heterogeneity in profiles of fear of progression among nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients. Consequently, this study aims to identify the latent profiles of fear of progression among nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients and to explore factors of these profiles, including sociodemographic characteristics, clinical characteristics, illness perception, and meaning in life.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A total of 296 nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients completed the sociodemographic and disease related questionnaire, fear of progression questionnaire-short form, brief illness perception questionnaire and purpose in life test. Latent profile analysis was used to explore the subgroups of fear of progression. The variables associated fear of progression sub-profiles were compared using chi-square test, Fisher's exact test, Kruskal-Wallis H test and multivariate logistic regression analysis.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text: The fear of progression among nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients can be categorized into three profiles: low, moderate, and high fear profiles. The results of the multivariate logistic regression showed that gender, age and initial diagnosis/recurrence were signifcant factors associated with the subgroups of fear of progression. Female patients, patients aged 18-30 years, and those with recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) were prone to high fear profile. The result indicated that the higher illness perception and lower meaning in life, the greater the likelihood of being classified into a higher fear profile.

sections.heading: Implications
sections.text: Three latent profiles of fear of progression exist in the nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients. Healthcare providers should develop and implement tailored strategies based on the characteristics of three profiles to alleviate fear of progression and maintain mental health.

items.title: Sedentary accumulation patterns and mental health among university teachers: longitudinal evidence from a single-university two-wave cohort.
items.authors: Zhang H, Huang Y, Wang S, Xiu L, Wang Y.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To examine whether 12-month changes in sedentary accumulation were associated with mental-health outcomes among university teachers while accounting for concurrent changes in total sitting time.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Full-time teachers ( n  = 769) completed 7-day activPAL4 monitoring and the World Health Organization-Five Well-Being Index (WHO-5), 10-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), and Maslach Burnout Inventory-Emotional Exhaustion (MBI-EE) at baseline and 12 months. Changes in mean sitting-bout length (MBL), the proportion of sitting time accumulated in bouts ≥30 min (Prolonged30%), and total sitting time were entered simultaneously in ANCOVA models adjusted for the corresponding baseline outcome, changes in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity and sleep quality, age, sex, and baseline BMI. Model 2 additionally adjusted for T1 levels of the three sedentary exposures.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: In Model 2, greater reductions in MBL were associated with higher WHO-5 scores ( β  = -0.236, 95% CI - 0.441 to -0.032; p  = 0.023) and lower MBI-EE scores ( β  = 0.125, 95% CI 0.034 to 0.217; p  = 0.007), while greater reductions in Prolonged30% were associated with lower PSS-10 scores ( β  = 0.043, 95% CI 0.006 to 0.079; p  = 0.022). Reductions in total sitting time were favorably associated with all three outcomes. An interquartile-range reduction in MBL corresponded to a 0.97-point higher WHO-5 score, about one-tenth of the ~10-point contextual reference value; the corresponding 0.44-point lower PSS-10 estimate for an interquartile-range reduction in Prolonged30% was about 16-20% of the 2.2-2.7-point contextual reference range. All semi-partial f ^2 values for focal predictors in the primary Model 2 analyses were <0.02.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: More favorable changes in sedentary accumulation were associated with better mental-health outcomes, but the estimated incremental effects were small. Because MBL is structurally linked to sitting volume and bout frequency, its associations are better interpreted as reflecting a more frequently interrupted pattern of sitting rather than an isolated effect of bout duration.

items.title: The association between family support and college students' well-being: an analysis of mediating pathways.
items.authors: Chai M, Su S, Wang Y, Shi J, Wang Q, Zhou S, Dong H, Wu B, Xu T.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The issue of student mental health represents a key concern for higher education institutions. Their well-being is associated with multiple factors, including family environment and institutional education. This study aims to explore the relationship between family support and student well-being, with mediating roles of school support and psychological capital.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This study employed a cross-sectional research design with a multi-stage stratified cluster sampling method to collect questionnaire data from 10,726 college students in Shandong Province, China. Core variables were measured using the Mental Health Continuum-Short Form (MHC-SF), the Family APGAR Index, the School Support Scale, and the Psychological Capital Scale. Independent samples t -tests and analysis of variance were used for comparative analyses, and multiple linear regression alongside structural equation modeling to investigate the associations between various factors and college students' well-being.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Significant differences in well-being scores were observed across academic year, major, program level, family structure, and parental workplace, both mother and father, at P < 0.05 multiple linear regression analysis showed that psychological capital, family support, and school support were all significantly positively correlated with college students' well-being scores. Among these, psychological capital was identified as a significant mediating variable in the model. Structural equation modeling (SEM) further revealed that the association between family support and well-being comprised both a direct path and indirect paths via school support and psychological capital.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: Overall, for students with diverse family backgrounds, there is a significant direct association between family support and well-being. In addition, this association can be realized through three indirect pathways: (1) an independent mediating pathway via school support, (2) an independent mediating pathway via psychological capital, and (3) a sequential mediating pathway via both school support and psychological capital. It is important to note that the measurement of psychological capital in this study employed a simplified operationalization based on positive emotion items as a proxy indicator for cognitive psychological resources; however, this measurement approach has limitations in terms of construct coverage, and this should be carefully considered when interpreting the research findings.

items.title: Differential effects of forest environmental perception on psychological well-being: the moderating role of perceived stress in national parks.
items.authors: Ni W, Li J.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The rapid urbanization and exposure to unnatural environments has helped to escalate global mental health problems. Interventions involving forests have been demonstrated to be therapeutic, but current studies are mostly concerned with direct effects, not taking into consideration environmental perception and individual differences. Specifically, the moderating effects of stress in determining the psychological well-being benefits of forest settings are not well studied. This study therefore examined whether perceived stress moderates the association between forest environmental perception and psychological well-being among adult visitors to a national park.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This quantitative cross-sectional study involved 300 adult visitors to Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, China. Recruitment continued until 300 eligible, consenting visitors completed the questionnaire. Ineligibility and refusal were resolved at the point of approach, before enrolment, and every questionnaire collected passed an on-site completeness check, so 300 was both the number collected and the number analysed, with no case excluded at the analysis stage. Because recruitment used non-probability purposive intercept sampling, the findings describe this visitor sample rather than a defined population, and all interval estimates are model-based rather than design-based. Validated measures were used to collect data on forest environmental perception, perceived stress (PSS-10), and psychological well-being (WHO-5). All instruments demonstrated acceptable internal consistency reliability (Cronbach's α > 0.70). SPSS and R were used to perform Pearson correlation and hierarchical regression analyses to test moderation, with the addition of an interaction term for forest environmental perception and stress.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Psychological well-being had a positive relationship with forest environmental perception ( r = 0.61, p < 0.001), and perceived stress was negatively related to it ( r = -0.55, p < 0.001). Regression analysis revealed that environmental perception had a significant and positive association with psychological well-being ( B = 21.50, p < 0.001), whereas perceived stress was negatively associated ( B = -1.53, p < 0.001). The interaction term was also significant ( B = -1.29, p < 0.001), indicating that perceived stress statistically moderated this association, with the conditional slope falling from B = 29.88 at low stress to B = 13.12 at high stress. Perceived stress was unrelated to forest environmental perception itself ( r = -0.05, p = 0.436). A significant amount of variance was explained by this model ( R ^2 = 0.714).

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: Because all variables were measured concurrently, no causal or temporal ordering is implied. The results indicate that the psychological well-being gains of forest environments are not limited to environmental perception but also depend on personal stress levels. Notably, the attenuation observed at high stress does not arise from stressed visitors appraising the forest less favourably, but occurs downstream of appraisal-in the conversion of a favourable appraisal into felt well-being. This pattern is consistent with stress-related constraints on attentional capacity, ruminative self-focus, and emotion regulation. This research adds a moderation-based framework to the literature and underscores the necessity of individually tailored nature-based interventions. Accordingly, we propose a three-tier scheme for national park management and public health practice, in which self-directed access, guided restorative programming, and clinically partnered repeated-dose provision are matched to low, moderate, and high visitor stress, respectively.
