items.title: Occupational stress, work-life balance, and coping among female veterinarians in Germany.
items.authors: Kolsch L, Ózsvári L, Máté M.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Veterinary medicine involves substantial emotional and ethical responsibilities that may contribute to psychological strain. Work-related stressors, including long working hours, euthanasia, client-related challenges, and moral conflicts, have been associated with burnout and reduced mental well-being. This exploratory study examined occupational stress, work-life balance, and coping strategies among female veterinarians in Germany in relation to demographic, professional, and workplace characteristics.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Given the gender composition of the veterinary workforce in Germany, with women representing the majority of veterinarians, this study focused on female veterinarians as a particularly relevant subgroup. An online questionnaire was distributed to veterinarians in Germany between September 2024 and September 2025. In total, 152 valid responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson's chi-square tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, and Kruskal-Wallis tests.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Working more than 40 h per week was associated with lower perceived workload manageability ( p  < 0.0001), less frequent conscious breaks, and more pronounced stress or burnout symptoms. Work-life balance showed the most consistent associations with stress- and recovery-related indicators: respondents with poor or very poor work-life balance reported lower workload manageability, less frequent conscious breaks, and more pronounced stress or burnout symptoms (all p  < 0.0001). Respondents most frequently relied on informal and adaptive coping strategies, particularly talking to friends or family (84.2%), hobbies or leisure activities (69.7%), and physical exercise (57.9%), whereas professional counseling or therapy was reported by 15.1%. Avoidance or ignoring stress was more common among respondents with poor or very poor work-life balance (χ2 = 7.433, p  < 0.05). Satisfaction with support for professional development and continuing education was associated with higher workload manageability, less pronounced stress or burnout symptoms, and more favorable ratings of team-based process optimization.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Overall, the findings suggest that occupational stress and coping patterns among female veterinarians are associated with working hours, work-life balance, professional experience, and support for professional development and continuing education. These results highlight the importance of systemic approaches, including manageable working hours, protected breaks, collegial support, mentoring, improved workplace communication, and accessible psychological support, for promoting sustainable mental health in veterinary medicine.

items.title: Cognitive impairment in idiopathic intracranial hypertension: A conceptual framework and therapeutic implications.
items.authors: Shin BJ, Suresh VA, Borg N.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Cognitive impairment is an increasingly recognized but poorly understood manifestation of idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH). Although deficits in attention, executive functioning, memory, processing speed, and reaction time have been reported, the characteristics, trajectory, and underlying mechanisms of cognitive dysfunction remain incompletely defined. Interpretation of the literature is limited by heterogeneity in study design, variability in neurocognitive assessment methods, and the absence of standardized cognitive outcome measures. Consequently, cognitive morbidity is overlooked in clinical practice and is not incorporated into treatment decision-making, which remains centered around visual outcomes and papilledema.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In this narrative review, we synthesize evidence from IIH studies and related disease models to examine the putative mechanisms underlying cognitive dysfunction and propose a conceptual framework for its pathogenesis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Cognitive dysfunction in IIH may arise through interactions between elevated intracranial pressure, cerebral venous hypertension, symptom-related amplifiers including chronic headache, sleep disturbance, pulsatile tinnitus, and psychiatric comorbidity, and broader biological and socioeconomic modifiers influencing cognitive vulnerability and recovery. This framework integrates current evidence and identifies potential pathways linking IIH to cognitive impairment.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Improved understanding of the cognitive effects of IIH may help improve recognition of cognitive dysfunction in clinical care. Recognition of cognition as a clinically meaningful and potentially treatment-responsive outcome may help inform future studies evaluating whether cognition has a role in treatment selection, particularly in patients without papilledema, in whom disease burden may currently be underestimated.
